title: Bioinformatics Analysis of LC-MS/MS Results
author: Lihui Li
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.upievke
materials: Cluster3.0 and the Java Treeview software were used to study protein relative expression data performing hierarchicalclustering analysis. Euclidean distance algorithm for similarity measure and average linkage clustering algorithm for clusteringwere selected when performing hierarchical clustering. A heatmap was created as a visual aid in addition to the dendrogram.

The protein–protein interaction information of the studied proteins was retrieved fromIntAct molecular interaction database by their genesymbols or STRING software. The results were downloaded in theXGMML format and imported into Cytoscape software to visualize and further analyze functionalprotein-protein interaction networks. Furthermore, to evaluate the importance of the protein in the PPI network, the degree of each protein wascalculated.

steps.title: Retrieve protein sequences
steps.instruction: Download the FASTA format protein sequences of all differentially expressed proteins from the UniProtKB database in batch.

steps.title: Run BLAST+ search
steps.instruction: Use NCBI BLAST+ to query each protein sequence against the database, retrieve the top 20 blast hits per query with an E‑value < 1 e‑3, and export the results for downstream annotation.

steps.title: Annotate with Blast2GO
steps.instruction: Load the BLAST results into Blast2GO version 10 (Version 3.3.5) to transfer functional annotation to the studied sequences, covering the three Gene Ontology categories: biological process, molecular function, and cellular component.

steps.title: Map GO terms
steps.instruction: Perform Gene Ontology (GO) mapping and annotation within Blast2GO for each protein using the retrieved blast hits.

steps.title: Map KEGG pathways
steps.instruction: Blast the same FASTA protein sequences against the online KEGG database (http://www.genome.jp/kegg/), then use KEGG 12 to map the proteins to metabolic pathways.

steps.title: Perform enrichment analysis
steps.instruction: Using the entire quantified protein annotation set as the background, test for over‑representation of GO terms (BP, MF, CC) and KEGG pathways with Fisher’s exact test.

steps.title: Adjust p‑values and filter
steps.instruction: Apply the Benjamini‑Hochberg correction for multiple testing to the derived p‑values and retain only functional categories and pathways with adjusted p‑values ≤ 0.05 as significant.
